leaves.name: gamma1IntegralSpan
leaves.doc: Shimura, Introduction to the arithmetic theory of automorphic functions (1971), Thm 3.52 (number UNVERIFIED; also Diamond-Im 1995 section 12.3, Diamond-Shurman section 6.5 for k = 2): S_k(Gamma_1(N)) has a basis of cusp forms whose Fourier coefficients at infinity are rational integers. Consequence taken: for k >= 2, S_k(Gamma_1(N)) (Mathlib CuspForm on Gamma1 N) is spanned over C by forms with integral q-expansion (period 1). With heckePrimeIntegralToRational it gives K_f a number field (coeff-field, coeff-rational; all glue proved).

leaves.name: heckePrimeIntegralToRational
leaves.doc:
The Hecke operators T_p preserve the integral structure, weakest form: for k >= 2 and a prime p not dividing N, Tau Ceti's T_p (the double coset Gamma_1(N) diag(1,p) Gamma_1(N), heckeSlashGamma1CuspFormEnd k (diagCosetGamma1 N p); Diamond-Shurman normalization a_m(T_p g) = a_{pm}(g) + p^(k-1) a_{m/p}(

g)) maps a cusp form on Gamma_1(N) with integral q-expansion to one with rational q-expansion. Source: the Hecke operators T_n preserve S_k(Gamma_1(N), Z) (Shimura 1971 section 3.5 with Thm 3.52; Diamond-Im 1995 sections 12.3-12.4; Diamond-Shurman section 6.5 for k = 2; locators UNVERIFIED). Consequence taken: p prime to N, integral input, rational output; T_p lies in the Hecke algebra in every convention, so no diamond-operator reading is needed (the diamond operators are derived: Dirichlet + Tau Ceti's recurrence, coeff-rational).
